release.name: Say Which Build
release.notes: The key window now carries the same footer bar the main window does: a Discord badge that copies the invite, and a chip that names the build. The key window is where both matter most -- it is the first thing a player sees, and when something is wrong it is often the only thing they see, so it is exactly where a player needs the invite within reach and where support needs to be able to ask "what does the chip say?" and get an answer that identifies the build. The chip shows two numbers because they answer two different questions: RvrseUI's own version says which UI is running, and the hub build id says which HUB -- and that second one decides whether the player's key is allowed to open it at all, which is the single most common cause of a key being refused. A hub still names its Discord invite ONCE: the default and the opt-out rule moved into UIHelpers.resolveDiscordInvite, read by both windows, because WindowBuilder already hands the key system the same config table. Two windows quietly disagreeing about the invite is a bug nobody reports -- players just stop finding the Discord.

changes: A REMEMBERED KEY NOW TELLS THE HUB. Every way a key succeeds calls OnKeyValid -- a typed key does, and so does the getgenv one-key bridge -- except the saved-key path, which returned true and said nothing. So anything a hub hangs on OnKeyValid worked on a player's FIRST launch and silently did nothing on every launch after it, once SaveKey had remembered the key. Found when a key gate validated a saved key, never heard about it, and left the player looking at an empty window.

The key window is now a window: it FITS THE SCREEN (a UIScale sized from the room there is -- it asked for 500 across on a phone that is 381 across, so it was cut off on the devices most players use), it MOVES (drag the header, clamped on-screen like the main window since 4.5.2), and it CLOSES (an X in the header).

SHUTDOWN: closing the key window, or running out of attempts, now fires the close hook on the window CreateWindow hands back. That hook was a no-op, so a hub auto-shutdown armed onto nothing and a player who closed the key screen left the hub loops running with nothing able to stop them. KeySystem.ClosedReason tells a closed window from a refused key.

FREE KEYS: the watcher no longer gives up after 5 minutes. The ads take 4-6 minutes and the provider sometimes offers a 60-minute wait instead, so the player was told the hub unlocks by itself and then had to come back and tap anyway. It checks every poll_after for 5 minutes, then every 20 seconds, until the SERVER says the run is over.
The key window releases everything it starts (its drag and fit listeners used to stay connected for the rest of the session), and a shake no longer teleports a dragged window back to the middle.

THE DUMMY WINDOW CAN NOW DO EVERYTHING A REAL ONE CAN. When a key is refused, or the player closes the key window, CreateWindow hands the hub a dummy window so its script does not explode -- but that dummy was missing SelectTab, SetTitle, Hide, SetIcon, SetTokenIcon and GetTokenIcon. On a real device, closing the key screen gave "attempt to call missing method 'SelectTab'", so every hub that calls it (UniversalHub v2 has since 4.5.1) crashed there -- and anything it meant to do afterwards, INCLUDING ARMING ITS SHUTDOWN, never ran. The `dummyparity` headless scenario now compares the dummy against a real window and fails if a method is ever added without one.

FIX: nothing prints with debug off. Five bare print() calls shipped always-on and showed in every hub user's console: 'UI visible - all settings applied', 'Window closed:', 'Interface destroyed', 'Successfully mounted to CoreGui' and 'All interfaces destroyed'. All five now go through the gated Debug.printf / dprint, so RvrseUI:EnableDebug(true) still shows them and nobody else does.

FIX: the window reveal ran twice on every launch. RvrseUI shows the window itself (the task.defer at the end of WindowBuilder) AND hubs are told to call Window:Show() last -- both correct, so Show() legitimately arrives twice. A rootRevealed guard means the particle burst, snapshotLayout('post-show') and the log now happen once per appearance; setHidden(true) clears it so hiding and showing again reveals properly. Measured: 2 reveals on 4.8.0, 1 on 4.8.1.
A configuration that would not load and a Notify that itself threw stay visible but moved to warn(), Roblox's channel for a problem rather than a line in everyone's output.
WindowManager gained the same gated dprint the other modules use, wired through WindowManager:Initialize({ Debug = Debug }); the argument is optional so older callers keep working.

Gate: the quiet scenario in tests/headless/run.js now allows ZERO prints with debug off instead of excusing three 'status' lines, and reports 'debug off: build=0 use=0'. The source guard's allow-list shrank to the gated helper alone. CLAUDE.md gained WARNING #0e so neither rule is undone.

The key window can hand out a free 24-hour key, paid for by ads. One button does the whole walk: asks the licence server for an ad link, copies it to the clipboard (an executor cannot open a browser), then watches for the key and fills it in. The player types nothing.

No hub has to build or configure any of this: any hub that already sets KeySettings.License gets the button, and a server with free keys switched off answers 'off', which makes the button take itself away. Opt out with License.FreeKey = false, which makes no server call at all.
A device that still holds a live free key is handed it straight back with no ad run, so a reinstall costs a player nothing and keys cannot be farmed.
New: KeySystem:StartFreeKey(license) and KeySystem:ClaimFreeKey(code, license) for anyone driving this themselves.

A full-lock LUAVM-Rvrse build cannot start until the licence server answers VALID -- that answer is literally what decrypts it. The build now leaves the answer in getgenv().LUAVM_LICENSE_OK and the key window takes its word for it, so a licensed launch asks the server ONCE instead of twice.
Only a receipt for the same key, marked VALID and under five minutes old, is trusted. A stale, mismatched, unstamped or non-VALID receipt falls back to a real server call exactly as before.

KeySettings.License = { Endpoint, BuildId, Secret } makes the key window ask a LUAVM-Rvrse licence server instead of checking a key list written into the file, so the valid keys never ship with the hub and the server enforces expiry, bans and one device per key.
It is Method 0 inside ValidateKey, so SaveKey, WebhookURL, MaxAttempts, OnKeyValid, OnKeyInvalid, OnAttemptsExhausted and the Get-Key button all keep working.

One key covers both the window and a full-lock build: the device id is computed exactly as the LUAVM loader computes it, and a key already in getgenv().LUAVM_LICENSE_KEY is checked silently so a buyer never types it twice.

🔝 FIX: game screens no longer cover RvrseUI. Its screens sat in PlayerGui at DisplayOrder 999 (100 in init.lua), so any game screen above that drew over the window and took its clicks. They now use the three largest orders (windows 2147483645, lists and colour panels 2147483646, the pointer 2147483647). They stay in PlayerGui, where hubs already out there look for the window (the X button, to hook their own shutdown).

🆕 CreateWindow{ AlwaysOnTop = true } moves RvrseUI's screens into the executor's hidden folder (gethui), else CoreGui. Roblox draws those above EVERY PlayerGui screen whatever its order (checked in Studio: a CoreGui screen at order 0 took the click over a PlayerGui screen at 2147483647), and the game's own scripts can't see them. A hub that asks for it must use Window:OnClose for its shutdown: a search of PlayerGui for the X no longer finds it. While Roblox's own Esc menu is open, RvrseUI's screens step aside there (Leave / Settings stay clickable) and come back when it closes. Where neither folder takes a screen (a plain game script) the screens stay in PlayerGui.

🛑 FIX: 2147483647 is the largest DisplayOrder and one more wraps round to the very bottom. The dropdown/colour-panel screen used to go 'one above the highest screen' and the dropdown fallback '+1000': both now stop below the largest order.

🖱️ NEW: while a window is on screen the mouse is free in first-person games (an invisible Modal button: Roblox unlocks the mouse itself and locks it again when the window is minimised or closed; the game's own mouse settings are never written). Only on a device with a mouse: a touch screen behaves exactly as before.

➚ NEW: where the game hid the pointer (MouseIconEnabled = false), RvrseUI draws Roblox's own arrow at the mouse while a window is on screen, above everything. It goes away when the game shows its pointer again.
⚙️ CreateWindow{ UnlockMouse = false } leaves the mouse and the pointer to the game.

📱 FIX: the window fits the screen. It asks for 580x480 (a touch screen held upright: 380x520) and takes at most the room below Roblox's top bar, less a margin. On a phone held sideways (about 750x381) the old fixed 380x520 window was tall and narrow, ran 140px off the bottom and sat in the top bar; now it is 580 wide and fits. A desktop still gets 580x480.

🔄 The window is fitted again when the screen changes size (a phone turned, a resized game window), and can't be dragged off the screen. A window opened where the last one was left is kept on the screen.

🏷️ FIX: a control's label is never covered by its control. On a narrow card the dropdown button, text box and key button give way (down to half the card); every label is cut with '...' instead of running under the control.
📝 FIX: Paragraph and Label cards are as tall as their text (they guessed 50 characters a line and cut the text on phones).

🎨 FIX: the colour picker panel opens on the right of the screen, centred top to bottom (it started 52px below the middle and ran off the bottom, on desktops too), drawn smaller on a screen too short for it; its rows are in order again (RGB, HSV, Hex Code: rows used to land among the titles).
📋 FIX: a dropdown list near the bottom of the screen stays on it (the bounds mixed screen and top-bar-shifted pixels and let it run off by the bar's height).
⌨️ FIX: the Keybind button can be seen (its highlight gradient hid the button and its text until clicked). On a touch screen with no keyboard a tap no longer waits for a key forever.
🆕 ColorPicker:SetOpen(state) opens or closes the picker panel from code, like a dropdown's SetOpen.

🆕 Window:SelectTab(target): switch tabs from code. target = position (1 = the first tab created), tab Title, or the tab CreateTab returned. Returns true/false; an unknown target warns and returns false, it never errors.
🐛 FIX: scripts that call Window:SelectTab(1) no longer stop with 'attempt to call a nil value' (the method did not exist).
🔇 ColorPicker diagnostics print only when debug is on (RvrseUI:EnableDebug(true)). Live on main since 2026-10-07, first listed here.

🧹 FIX: Closing a window no longer leaves RvrseUI running. Before, every close path left ~38 live connections (global input listeners per Slider/Dropdown/Keybind/ColorPicker, the window and chip drag listeners, a per-frame Heartbeat for the chip shine and the particle loop) plus the overlay ScreenGui. Now: zero.
🪟 FIX: Closing one window no longer destroys every other RvrseUI window (the X used to destroy the shared host). The last window to close still removes everything.
🧩 FIX: Dropdown lists and ColorPicker panels that are open in the overlay layer at close time are removed with their window.
🔁 One teardown path for the X button, Window:Destroy(), RvrseUI:Destroy() and the destroy key. Window:Destroy() no longer yields; closing twice is harmless.
🆕 Window:OnClose(fn) / CreateWindow{ OnClose = fn } — runs once with the reason ("close-button", "destroy", "destroy-key", "rvrseui-destroy") however the window closes.
🆕 Window:Track(item) — hand RvrseUI a connection, thread, Instance or cleanup function; it is released when the window closes.
🆕 Window:IsDestroyed().

🆕 CreateWindow{ TurnOffTogglesOnClose = true } — every ON toggle runs its own OnChanged(false) on close so features switch themselves off; a per-toggle TurnOffOnClose overrides it. Saved configs keep the ON state.

🔨 BUILD FIX: tools/build.js and tools/build.lua wrap each module in do...end again (as the v4.3.x monolith did). Without it, WindowBuilder.lua's private `local Theme, Obfuscation, ...` shadowed the real modules and the monolith died at load with "attempt to index nil with Initialize" — the 4.4.x executor breakage. build.lua now matches build.js byte-for-byte (it also missed FilterableList).

🧪 NEW tests/headless (node tests/headless/run.js): runs the real RvrseUI.lua in a strict fake Roblox client. 9 close scenarios (X, Window:Destroy, RvrseUI:Destroy, destroy key, two windows, open overlays, reopen after close, TurnOffTogglesOnClose with config saving, Window:Track) — 0 leftover connections, 0 ScreenGuis, 0 errors.

Added: a Discord badge above the version badge, 16x16, which copies the invite on click and says so in a notification (the notification repeats the invite in full, so a player whose executor has no clipboard at all still has something to read).

Added: CreateWindow options DiscordInvite (a hub's own link, or false to opt out; naming nothing carries the library default) and DiscordIcon (defaults to icon://chat, accepts any icon the library resolves).
Added: UIHelpers.copyText, now the only clipboard implementation in the library.

Fixed: the clipboard search read the environment with rawget, so it missed every executor that serves setclipboard through a metatable -- which looked exactly like an executor that cannot copy. This was in the key window's ad-link hand-off, where it costs the player a free key.

Tests: harness scenario 'discord' (badge present, above the version badge, tiny, draws something, a hub's own invite wins, no invite named carries the library default, and DiscordInvite = false shows no badge) and licence scenarios 'adlink' / 'adlink_meta' (the ad link reaches the clipboard, including through a metatable). All verified by mutation.

Added: a footer bar on the KEY window, carrying the same pair the main window has -- a Discord badge that copies the invite, and a chip naming the build. The key window is the first thing a player sees and often the only thing they see when something is wrong.

Added: the build chip shows RvrseUI's version and, when KeySettings.License.BuildId is set, the first 8 characters of the hub's build id. Tapping it copies the full line (version, build, hash, channel, hub build id) because a player reading an 11px chip aloud gets it wrong.

Added: UIHelpers.resolveDiscordInvite and UIHelpers.DEFAULT_DISCORD_INVITE -- ONE definition of the invite and the opt-out rule, read by both windows. A hub names DiscordInvite once in CreateWindow and the key window honours it with no extra plumbing, because WindowBuilder already passes the same config table to KeySystem:Process.

Changed: the key window footer uses its own geometry rather than the main window's. The main bar is sized off the tab rail (railWidth) and the key window has no rail -- it is a 500-wide dialog -- so sharing those numbers would wedge a tab-shaped bar into a dialog. The invite and the clipboard are shared; the geometry deliberately is not.
Changed: KeySystem now receives the Version module, so the key window can name the build it belongs to.
